issue_context.summary: The same backup_restore_settings.json is copied into many module and plugin output folders even though runtime code only needs it for Settings.
known_information: The issue lists duplicated files across module and launcher plugin directories.
A recent installation inventory in the local checkout still shows the same file in many output folders.
Settings.UI.Library.csproj marks the JSON as CopyToOutputDirectory=PreserveNewest.
inferences: Because many executables/plugins reference Settings.UI.Library, the content item propagates transitively into each output instead of only the Settings app output.
issue_context.analysis: The current project file and current installation inventory confirm the original packaging bug remains. The fix can make the data an embedded/library resource or copy it explicitly only from the Settings application packaging project.
initial_investigation: SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils reads either backup_restore_settings.json or Settings\backup_restore_settings.json from the working directory.
No pull request referencing issue 26715 was found.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Start the bounded fork-side design workflow. This draft performs no upstream write.

proposed_fixes.title: Stop transitive backup/restore manifest copies
proposed_fixes.root_cause: backup_restore_settings.json is an output content item of Settings.UI.Library, so every consuming executable copies it into its own output/install directory.
plan: Move the JSON copy item from the shared library to the Settings application/package that owns backup and restore.
Prefer embedding the manifest in Settings.UI.Library or resolve it through an explicit Settings install path rather than Environment.CurrentDirectory.
Add packaging assertions that exactly one intended installed copy exists and backup/restore still loads it in packaged and local builds.
verification: Build/install PowerToys, inventory backup_restore_settings.json locations, and run Settings backup and restore in packaged and local configurations.

confidence.rationale: The current csproj directly explains the duplicated current installation output.
